content: Administer 768 mg orally twice daily. Continue treatment for two years or until disease recurrence or unacceptable toxicity occurs. If hemoglobin levels drop below 8 g/dL, withhold the medication until recovery to at least 8 g/dL, then resume at the same dose. If anemia recurs (hemoglobin < 8 g/dL), withhold the medication again until recovery to at least 8 g/dL, then resume at the next reduced dose level. Ornidyl (eflornithine) is contraindicated in patients with hypersensitivity to eflornithine or any component of the formulation. The World Health Organization supplies Ornidyl to the CDC for use in treating African trypanosomiasis. Based on findings from animal studies and its mechanism of action, fetal harm may occur if administered to pregnant females. Verify pregnancy status in females of reproductive potential before initiating treatment. There are no available data on the use of eflornithine in pregnant females. Inform pregnant females and females of reproductive potential about the potential fetal risks. There is no data on the presence of eflornithine in human breast milk, its effects on breastfed children, or its impact on milk production. Advise women not to breastfeed during treatment and for one week after the last dose. Category A: Generally acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. Administer the medication with or without food. Tablets may be swallowed whole, chewed, or crushed. Store the medication at 20–25°C (68–77°F), with permissible excursions between 15–30°C (59–86°F).
